mentions.name: Local Airfield Runway Tracking Tool
mentions.description: This tool records takeoffs and landings at a local single-runway airfield and determines which runway direction is used for each operation, to check whether the airfield follows its stated wind-based runway assignment rules. It polls for aircraft within a 5 km circle every 30 seconds, tracks candidates every 5 seconds, infers takeoff/landing and runway direction from coordinates and altitude, enriches the data with wind speed/direction from a weather API, saves results to JSON, and displays them in a frontend table. Built with Express and TypeScript, currently a working prototype in bug-fixing, with plans to open source it.
mentions.problem: Free aircraft APIs don't register landing/takeoff events or runway assignments, and the local airfield's single runway operated in both directions causes noise complaints in a densely populated area; the tool exists to verify whether the airfield follows its own runway assignment rules and whether the noise annoyance is justified.
mentions.source_excerpt: Working on a flight tracking tool that records the landing and takeoff actions of a local airfield to get insights in how they determine on which runway a takeoff or landing is assigned.
